organization: American Trucking Associations — Moving and Storage Conference
document_title: Code of Ethics (Moving and Storage Conference)
notes: ATA Moving & Storage Conference division code. Main ATA national body does not publish a general trucking driver code of ethics. This is the most explicit ethics document found for US land transport.

profession_name: Public Transit Executive / Transit Agency Officer
notes: Applies to APTA officers, directors, and committee chairs. Covers legal compliance, antitrust, meeting conduct, harassment-free environment. Board-approved policy. Not a code for bus drivers or transit workers — governance level only.

organization: Nautilus International / RMT / UK Chamber of Shipping
document_title: Code of Conduct for the Merchant Navy
profession_name: Seafarer / Merchant Navy Officer and Rating
notes: Published May 13, 2019. Agreed between Nautilus International, RMT, and UK Chamber of Shipping; approved by the Maritime & Coastguard Agency. Sets disciplinary rules and procedures for seafarers during shipboard employment. Recognizes unique demands of seafaring. Aligned with 2016 MLC amendments on harassment/bullying. PDF: https://alphamarine.ie/assets/PDFs/Code-of-Conduct-for-the-Merchant-Navy.pdf

ILO Convention C186. Entered into force August 20, 2013; amended 2016 (harassment/bullying). Fourth pillar of international maritime law. Covers seafarer rights, working conditions, fair treatment. Code of conduct compliance affects promotion rights. Binding on flag states. Not a professional association ethics code but the primary international normative framework for seafarer conduct.

IMPA Resolutions updated July 2023. No dedicated standalone code of ethics; professional standards expressed through Resolutions and guidance including Master-Pilot Exchange guidance, Diversity and Inclusion Guidance for Pilotage. Public interest served by regulated pilotage free of commercial pressure is a core principle.

document_title: Code of Ethics for IMO Personnel
notes: Effective date January 1, 2012 (Council adopted as Annex I to Service Code at 193rd Session). Internal staff code, not a seafarer code. Covers loyalty, independence, impartiality, integrity, zero tolerance for fraud/corruption, prohibition on gifts, prohibition on harassment. Applies to all IMO officials. Based on ICSC Standards of Conduct for International Civil Service.

Updated version announced 2024/2025. One of the most comprehensive union-based professional ethics codes in any sector. Canons cover: passenger safety as first responsibility; faithful discharge of duties; command responsibility; conduct on and off duty; no malicious injury to other pilots' reputation; reporting professional incompetence to ALPA. Professional Standards Committee (~500 trained members) processes cases. Represents 79,000+ pilots.

document_title: Professional Air Traffic Controller's Code / NATCA Code of Conduct
notes: Professional Air Traffic Controller's Code poster (2020) covers: personal commitment to safety and public trust; inspiring professionalism in others; airspace safety as greatest priority; individual actions representing the whole profession. Code of Conduct covers harassment/discrimination-free environment. Professional Standards Committee processes thousands of cases. Controller's Code poster: https://www.natca.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/08/ATC-Code-Poster.pdf

organization: International Federation of Air Line Pilots' Associations
notes: Represents 160,000+ pilots in 70+ countries. Founded 1948, Montreal-based. Written code focuses on organizational conduct/harassment-free environment at IFALPA events. Professional pilot conduct is deferred to member associations (e.g., ALPA). Safety policies implicitly address ethics. No standalone professional ethics code for in-flight conduct published.

organization: Association of Flight Attendants – Communications Workers of America
notes: Primarily a union officer ethics code: officers/representatives shall not receive compensation from employer boards; prohibition on personal payments from employers; prohibition on entering management negotiations without MEC President knowledge; prohibition on converting union property to personal use. Operational professional standards handled through EAP/Professional Standards Program.

Applies to all IATA employees and subsidiaries worldwide and, as far as possible, to consultants, contractors, suppliers, and other business partners. Highest standards of ethical conduct and social responsibilities. Not a code governing airline operations or crew conduct — organizational ethics framework for the world's leading airline trade body (representing 290+ airlines).

document_title: Aviators Model Code of Conduct (AMCC), Version 3
notes: Version 3 released 2022. Peer-reviewed volunteer initiative; endorsed by FAA resources. Covers operating practices to enhance quality and safety; flight and ground safety; professionalism; good judgment, ethical behavior, personal responsibility; improved communication between pilots, regulators, and aviation community. Provided free as public service. Repository: https://repository.fit.edu/amccenglish/

document_title: Principles and Standards of Ethical Supply Management Conduct
notes: Regularly reviewed by ISM Ethical Standards Committee. Core ethical principles: integrity, value, loyalty. Standards cover: preventing unethical conduct; avoiding conflicts of interest; protecting confidential information; avoiding improper reciprocal agreements; obeying laws and trade agreements; developing professional skills. Applied through ISM certification programs.

organization: Chartered Institute of Procurement and Supply
notes: 2024 version; significant amendments from 2014 onward. Five commitments: (1) enhance and protect profession standing; (2) maintain highest integrity in business relationships; (3) promote eradication of unethical practices including modern slavery and corruption; (4) enhance professional proficiency; (5) ensure legal compliance. Formal Disciplinary Committee; sanctions range from reprimand to expulsion. Royal Charter authority. Online ethics test since 2014. Professional Register for public verification.

organization: Supply Chain Management Association / Supply Chain Canada
document_title: SCMA Code of Ethics for Professionals in the Field of Supply Chain Management
notes: Reviewed minimum every 5 years. Covers professional judgment, conflict of interest disclosure, no misrepresentation of credentials, compliance with professional standards. Sanctions include reprimand, letter of censure; censured members barred from office for one year. Web: https://scma.com/on/about/code-of-ethics

organization: National Customs Brokers and Forwarders Association of America
notes: Code embedded within NCBFAA bylaws rather than as standalone published document. Core values: professionalism based on integrity, principles, ethics, and trust. Required adherence for Certified Customs Specialists (CCS). Represents 1,422+ member companies with 110,000 employees. Founded 1897. Bylaws PDF: https://members.ncbfaa.org/4DCGI/cms/review.html?Action=CMS_Document&DocID=8574
